tips.supersets: Supersets of opposing muscles, like bench press and rows in turn, save a lot of time without costing performance.
tips.dropSets: Drop sets build about as much muscle as regular sets, in much less time.
tips.reserve: At 10+ reps, most people underestimate how many reps they have left. There’s usually more in the tank than you think.
tips.setsPerSession: Past about 6 hard sets for a muscle in one workout, each extra set adds little. Spread them over two days instead.
tips.overheadTriceps: In one study, overhead triceps extensions grew the triceps about 40 % more than cable pushdowns.
tips.seatedLegCurl: Seated leg curls build more muscle than lying ones: the hamstrings are stretched further.
tips.deepSquats: Deep squats build clearly more glute than half squats.
tips.deadliftStance: In the deadlift, the bar starts over the middle of your foot, about 2–3 cm (1 in) in front of your shins.
tips.longerRest: In one study, muscles grew more with 3 minutes of rest than with 1, for the same number of sets.
tips.iceBath: An ice bath right after training can slow muscle growth. Save it for rest days.
tips.recoveryTime: A hard-trained muscle needs about 48–72 hours to perform at its best again.
tips.cardioOrder: Cardio and weights on the same day? Weights first, then cardio, ideally a few hours apart.
tips.proteinFood: 250 g of Greek yogurt has about 25 g of protein, as much as 4 eggs.
tips.casein: 30–40 g of casein before bed, e.g. cottage cheese, feeds your muscles through the night.
tips.creatine: Creatine takes 3–4 weeks to work fully. The time of day doesn’t matter, only that you take it every day.
tips.deficitProtein: In a calorie deficit you need more protein, not less: up to 2.2 g per kg of body weight (1 g per lb).
tips.salt: After a salty dinner, the scale often shows 1 kg (2 lb) more the next morning. That’s water, not fat.
tips.glycogen: Every gram of stored carbs holds about 3 g of water. That’s why the scale jumps after pizza night.
tips.fatKcal: A kilo of body fat holds about 7,000 kcal. A 500 kcal daily deficit is about a kilo (2 lb) in two weeks.
tips.doubleProgression: Stuck at a weight? First add 2 reps at that weight. Then it’s time for the next step up.
tips.mobility: Lifting makes you stiff? Training through the full range makes you about as flexible as stretching does.
tips.age: Too old to lift? In studies, even people in their 90s more than doubled their strength.
tips.spotReduction: Ab exercises to burn belly fat? You lose fat all over your body, not where you train.
tips.anabolicWindow: A shake within 30 minutes after training? How much protein you eat over the day matters far more.
tips.swap: Machine taken? Swap the exercise mid-workout for a matching alternative.
tips.plates: When you log a set, Loqqa shows which plates go on each side of the bar.
tips.kai: Ask Kai why your bench press has stalled. He answers with your own data.
